Independent METR measurements corroborated capability progress. The developer slowdown study is an important limit: progress did not make every application more productive. limitations: Support uses the ordinary directional reading, not a claim that every successor or application improved.
The interpretation of more extensive applications as expanded demonstrated workflows is material.
Company error measurements are not independent replications.

our_interpretation: Because Marcus explicitly re-endorses the earlier quotation, I read next generation relative to January 7, 2025.
The ordinary reading predicts directional progress in the successor generation, rather than improvement by every model on every task.

Greater abilities means improved measured task performance; more extensive applications means demonstrated expansion of usable workflows; somewhat mitigate means a measured reduction in at least some existing failure modes.
No deadline is supplied. The forecast does not require AGI, elimination of hallucinations, or universal productivity gains.
criteria.support_condition: Released successor systems demonstrate improved capabilities, expanded usable workflows, and measured reductions in existing weaknesses compared with predecessors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A clearly identified successor generation, comprehensively evaluated on comparable tasks and practical workflows, fails to improve the claimed dimensions or shows the opposite overall pattern. Mere delay is insufficient.

evidence.locator: Building responsibly; capability and deployment details in Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code sections
evidence.explanation: Anthropic reports improved capabilities and fewer unnecessary refusals relative to the predecessor. It also describes Claude Code's release and practical coding deployments, providing concrete evidence of expanded workflows rather than only benchmark scores.

evidence.excerpt: GPT‑5 is significantly less likely to hallucinate than our previous models.
evidence.locator: More accurate answers to real-world queries; Evaluations
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports improved capability evaluations and approximately 45% fewer responses containing factual errors than GPT-4o on representative production prompts with browsing enabled. Together with the earlier Claude release, this establishes progress across two successor families, including mitigation of a weakness highlighted in Marcus's post.

The study independently documents increasing task-completion horizons through Claude 3.7 Sonnet. Its software and reasoning tasks corroborate capability progress, while a 50% success threshold does not establish dependable performance in every deployment.

Experienced developers working in familiar repositories were slower with the tested early-2025 tools. This limits any claim of universal practical improvement, but does not contradict the narrower forecast of some expanded applications and partial mitigation of weaknesses.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The GPT-5 release supplied a second major successor family with capability and factuality improvements. Combined with e1's expanded workflows and reduced refusals and e3's independent capability measurements, the dated record meets all three parts of the early-resolution rule.
